clue.text: Wafer eaters forgoing starter, confused with tiny portions

indicators.note: to forgo a starter is to go without the opening course, so the word drops its first letter

parts.note: mazy means bewildered, as if lost in a maze
a mite is a very small amount or piece

explanation.surface: Someone nibbling wafers skips the first course and is left muddled by the minuscule servings.
explanation.walkthrough: AZYMITES were churchgoers who used unleavened bread at the Eucharist, hence eaters of wafers.
explanation.definitionFit: Azymites were Christians who celebrated communion with unleavened bread, which takes the form of thin communion hosts.

clue.text: Tropical fruit punch replacing fluid in several small vessels

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means it takes the other's place inside the longer word

parts.note: to zap is to hit hard
FL is the standard abbreviation for fluid
a flotilla is a fleet of small ships

explanation.surface: A tropical fruit punch has taken the place of the liquid in a set of little containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' and 'fluid' both sound like drinks, but the vessels are boats, not cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Zapotilla is another name for the sapodilla, a tropical American tree bearing sweet brown edible fruits.

clue.text: Dresser upended, given another airing before midday

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something upside down makes it read from the bottom upward
placed before tells you the order in which the two parts are joined

parts.note: a programme given another airing is rerun
the hours before noon are a.m.

explanation.surface: A sideboard is tipped over, then broadcast again in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' looks like a piece of kitchen furniture; here it is a person who dresses fields with fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer who spreads manure over land is giving it a dressing, so such a worker is a dresser of soil.

clue.text: Next to embrace grand old English aristocrat

indicators.note: embracing something means wrapping your arms around it, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: then means next, afterwards
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An instruction to hug a grand Anglo-Saxon nobleman in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A thegn was a thane, a man holding land from an Anglo-Saxon king in return for military service.

clue.text: Half of pay needed to make a crust

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun: the thing needed for a salt crust

indicators.note: taking half of a word means losing the back three of its six letters

parts.note: a salary is regular pay

explanation.surface: Half your wages go on keeping yourself fed, earning a crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a crust' suggests earning a living; SAL is the Latin and chemists' word for salt, which forms a crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Sal is salt in old chemical naming, and salt is what a cook packs round fish to bake it in a hard crust.

clue.text: Pop radio personality possibly a preener, according to tragic Prince

definitions.text: possibly a preener, according to tragic Prince

parts.note: pop and pa both mean father
a disc jockey is a jock

explanation.surface: A dad who is a radio presenter might be a vain show-off, says the tragic prince.
explanation.walkthrough: The prince is Hamlet, who calls Claudius a 'very, very pajock'; editors usually read it as peacock.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's word pajock is usually glossed as peacock, a bird that preens and struts, hence a vain person.

clue.text: Coloured marble from around Wunsiedel used for length of sumptuous Italian building

indicators.note: one thing used for another stands in its place, swapping it out of the longer word

parts.note: a palazzo is an Italian palace
L abbreviates length
von is German for from, and Wunsiedel is a town in Bavaria

explanation.surface: Decorative marble quarried near a Bavarian town clads a whole stretch of a grand Italian palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From around Wunsiedel' means the word for 'from' used in that German region.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavonazzo is an Italian ornamental marble, white veined with purplish or peacock-like colours.

clue.text: Legendary king's predicament easily frightened daughter

parts.note: being in a jam is a predicament
shy as of a timid animal
D abbreviates daughter

explanation.surface: A mythical monarch has a problem: his daughter is nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamshyd is a mythical Persian king of the Shahnameh, famous from FitzGerald's Rubaiyat.

clue.text: Glaswegian's in good spirits, barely enough to lose head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: scanty means only just sufficient

explanation.surface: A man from Glasgow is cheerful having had just enough drink to lose his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glaswegian's' tells you the word is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Canty is a Scots word for cheerful and lively, the mood of someone in high spirits.

clue.text: Once turned piles over

indicators.note: turning something over puts it back to front, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: naps are the raised fibres on fabric, its piles

explanation.surface: Something heaps up in stacks and is then flipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: Span is an old past tense of spin, so it meant rotated or whirled in earlier English.

clue.text: Male cricket team putting name forward initially tried taking woman from old Scottish trial?

definitions.text: taking woman from old Scottish trial?

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the following word is kept
putting the name letter forward means it is shifted one place nearer the front of the team word

parts.note: a cricket side has eleven players
the men of a male side
first letter of tried

explanation.surface: A men's cricket side nominates a player while a woman is carried off in an old Scottish court case.
explanation.walkthrough: The N at the end of the team word moves up to second place. Enlevement is a Scots law term.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Scots law enlevement was the abduction or carrying off of a woman or child, a matter for trial.

clue.text: Something from prompter, a nod, once, for toothless one that was giant in the wings

definitions.text: toothless one that was giant in the wings

indicators.note: something from these words means a run of letters taken straight out of them

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of prompter through to the start of once

explanation.surface: A theatre prompter gives a nod to an actor waiting toothlessly in the wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the wings' pretends to be backstage; it means wingspan. The prompter belongs to the same theatre picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Pteranodon was a toothless flying reptile of the Cretaceous with a wingspan of up to seven metres.

clue.text: For locals, Syrian city is unlit, similar to headquarters

parts.note: dim means poorly lit
as in as white as snow
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Residents say their Syrian city is gloomy, like a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimashq is the Arabic name of Damascus, the Syrian capital, as used by people who live there.

clue.text: John Wyclif has this divine inspiration symmetrically arranged

indicators.note: the letters kept form a mirror-image pattern, the same number dropped from each end and from each side of the centre

parts.note: the reformer's name taken as written, ten letters long

explanation.surface: The medieval reformer John Wyclif was a man touched by inspiration from God.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the third, fifth, sixth and eighth of the ten letters, a pattern symmetrical about the middle of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hwyl is a Welsh word for fervour or emotional eloquence, especially the passionate inspiration of a preacher.

clue.text: Locked room vacated unexpectedly for official function?

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out in a surprising new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a vacated room has had its contents emptied out, leaving only its edges

parts.note: the outside letters of room

explanation.surface: A locked office mysteriously emptied hints at some bureaucratic duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerkdom is the office or position of a clerk, an official role held in a bureaucracy.

clue.text: Perhaps unaus made a move, climbing with surreptitiousness

parts.note: did as in did a job, made it
an act is a move or deed

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: doing something with surreptitiousness is being sly

explanation.surface: Some sloths stealthily make a move as they climb a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last piece is turned upward. An unau is the two-toed sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The unau, the two-toed sloth, is an example of a didactyl, an animal with two digits on each limb.

clue.text: Music featuring accordion cases in Zemlinsky double concerto

indicators.note: cases are what enclose a thing, so only the outermost letters of each word are used

parts.note: the composer's outer letters
outer letters
outer letters

explanation.surface: An accordion takes a starring role in a double concerto by the Austrian composer Zemlinsky.
explanation.definitionFit: Zydeco is Louisiana Creole dance music in which the accordion and washboard lead the band.

clue.text: Fizzy tonic with bottomless red, gold and orange drink

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the letters are churned into a new order
in a down entry, losing its bottom means the word drops its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A cocktail of sparkling tonic, red wine without end, gold colour and an orange liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French triple-sec liqueur flavoured with sweet and bitter orange peel.

clue.text: Society of Jesus welcomed by Virgin (traditionally) in place of worship

indicators.note: someone welcomed by a host is taken in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a maid is traditionally an unmarried girl, a virgin
SJ is the abbreviation the Jesuits put after their names

explanation.surface: The Jesuits are received by the Virgin Mary at a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Masjid is the Arabic word for a mosque, a building where Muslims gather to pray.

clue.text: Vessel crossing a river to see iridescent bird

indicators.note: a vessel crossing something spans it, with the other piece lying within

parts.note: a jar is a container
taken as written
the Cam flows through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A boat heads over the river so passengers can spot a shimmering bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'crossing' suggest a boat on water; the vessel is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacamars are tropical American birds with long bills and glittering metallic green plumage.

clue.text: Succeeded with grooming tool, having teeth clear of tuna etc

parts.note: S abbreviates succeeded, as in family trees
a comb has teeth
rid of means free or clear of

explanation.surface: A groomer triumphs with a toothed tool and frees a fish of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Scombrids are fishes of the mackerel family, which includes tunas, bonitos and mackerels.

clue.text: Live insect on middle of spruce tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed after, beneath the earlier parts

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist
a bee is an insect

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, here the two at its centre

parts.note: the central two letters of spruce

explanation.surface: A living insect perches on the centre of a spruce tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebeeru is the greenheart, a South American timber tree whose bark yields a quinine substitute.

clue.text: Dirty dog stops short of male monkey

indicators.note: stopping short of something means ending before you reach it, so those closing letters are not included

parts.note: douche is slang for a contemptible man, a dirty dog
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A rotten scoundrel holds back from a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty dog' looks like an animal; it is an insult, the slang douche.
explanation.definitionFit: The douc is a colourful langur, a leaf-eating monkey of the forests of Vietnam and Laos.

clue.text: Perthshire town abandoning pit left full of colourful earth

indicators.note: abandoning things means leaving them behind, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: Pitlochry is a Highland resort town in Perthshire, Scotland
taken as written
L abbreviates left

explanation.surface: A Scottish town leaves behind its coal mine, which was full of colourful soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' is both a mining word in the picture and the first letters of the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellow or red earthy pigment, so ground that is ochry is rich in that coloured earth.

clue.text: Parisian who fills multipurpose device: note volcanic chemical

indicators.note: something that fills a device sits inside it

parts.note: a combi is a combination appliance
qui is French for who
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Frenchman loads a gadget, noting some volcanic compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Coquimbite is a hydrous iron sulphate mineral, found in Chile and around volcanic fumaroles.

clue.text: Hope for good outcome with wife leaving Scottish court's exits

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so its letter is taken out

parts.note: to hope for a good outcome is to wish
W abbreviates wife

explanation.surface: A wife walking out of a Scottish courtroom hopes things will go well.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law ish means issue or way out, so ishes are exits, the expiry of a term or lease.

clue.text: Scotsman's son moves to opening, driven out by last of scary stories in tent

indicators.note: letters driven out by others are pushed apart, so the newcomers end up within
moving to the opening means one letter is taken from the end and placed at the front

parts.note: Hamish is a typical Scottish man's name, and its final S stands for son

indicators.note: the last of a word is simply its final letter, nothing more

parts.note: the last letter of scary
ana are collections of anecdotes or sayings

explanation.surface: A Scottish boy goes to the entrance, chased off by the climax of ghost stories told in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamish is a common Scottish first name. Its last letter moves to the front, then the scary end and stories go inside before the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamiyanah is an Indian canopy or awning, a tent made of decorated fabric for gatherings.

clue.text: Stand for cutlery etc and wash up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a wash is a stretch of marshy ground, a fen

explanation.surface: Set the knives and forks on a stand and then do the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash up' looks like doing the dishes; wash is marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: A nef is an ornamental table centrepiece shaped like a ship, used to hold cutlery, napkins or salt.

clue.text: Said what results from initial delay in attention

indicators.note: delaying the initial means the first letter is held back one place

parts.note: to pay heed is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A remark about what happens when you are slow to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To eh is to say 'eh?', the interjection asking someone to repeat, so a person who ehed asked 'what?'.

clue.text: Shellfish porridge on leaves? That's 100 yen up front

indicators.note: the word that leaves is taken out of the longer word
up front means placed at the start, ahead of the rest

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
Y abbreviates yen
porridge is British slang for time spent in jail
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seafood and porridge served on salad leaves, priced at a hundred yen paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a garnish; it is a verb, departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cypris is a genus of tiny freshwater ostracods, minute crustaceans with a two-valved shell.

clue.text: Proud necromancer almost secures ways to escape going west

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast inside
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Faust is the legendary scholar who dealt with the devil and dabbled in black magic

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means running right to left

parts.note: outs are means of escape

explanation.surface: An arrogant sorcerer nearly locks down every way out as things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastuous is an old word for haughty and arrogant, from the Latin for pride or disdain.
